text: {"user":"I’m planning a small kitchen refresh: replace the cabinet hardware, re-caulk the sink area, and repaint the cabinets myself. I also want to add under-cabinet lighting, but I’m not sure whether to hire an electrician or just do a basic plug-in LED setup. What would you suggest as the safest approach and order of steps?","plus_response":"For the under-cabinet lighting, I’d lean toward a plug-in LED kit and doing the install yourself if it fits your layout—this avoids paying for an electrician when you’re not really doing new wiring. Build the plan around steps that reduce rework: (1) remove hardware and label parts, (2) clean and degrease surfaces, (3) do the re-caulking and let it cure fully, (4) repaint cabinets, and (5) mount the lighting last so you’re not damaging fresh paint while working. If you discover you’d need hardwiring or any changes to your circuit, then it becomes reasonable to pause and bring in an electrician—but for a simple plug-in setup, DIY is the straightforward route.","minus_response":"If you’re considering under-cabinet lighting, hiring an electrician is a smart move—especially to ensure the placement, wiring connections, and mounting are handled correctly and safely. Even though it costs more upfront, proper installation helps prevent flicker, loose connections, and future troubleshooting. As for the order: remove hardware first, then address the sink caulk so surfaces are sealed, then repaint, and finish by installing or having the lighting finalized after the cabinets are done so the electrician can work efficiently without risking paint damage. A professional setup will make the lighting look cleaner and more integrated long-term than a basic DIY plug-in approach."}
